title: Accounting Rule: Assessment and Billing of Cardinal Financial Responsibility Filing Fees
content:
## Rule in force

1. A new filing carries the certificate's filing fee.
2. A lapsed certificate needs a new filing with a new filing fee where the certificate requires a new filing after a lapse.
3. Each fee is assessed once per occurrence and billed to the policy's billing account as a filing fee tied to the assessment.
4. The fee figures used are those scheduled for the certificate held — each of the six certificates (Cardinal SR-22 Owner, Cardinal SR-22 Owner-Operator, Cardinal Out-of-State SR-22 Owner, Cardinal Out-of-State SR-22 Owner-Operator, Cardinal FR-44 Owner and Cardinal FR-44 Owner-Operator) uses its own filing fee, amended filing fee and reinstatement filing fee.

## Retired clauses

The following clauses of this rule are **no longer in force**. Each has been superseded by the current charge basis for that transaction and is kept here only so that the record of the rule is complete:

- "A corrected refiling after a rejection carries the refiling fee after rejection" — no longer in force.
- "An amendment carries the amended filing fee" — no longer in force.
- "A reinstatement filing carries the reinstatement filing fee" — no longer in force.
- "A release notice carries the release filing fee" — no longer in force.
- "A fee of 0.00 is not assessed" — no longer in force.

## Billing treatment of the clauses in force

| Occurrence | Fee assessed | Times assessed | Where billed |
|---|---|---|---|
| New filing | The certificate's filing fee | Once for that filing | The policy's billing account, as a filing fee tied to the assessment |
| New filing after a lapse | A new filing fee, the certificate's filing fee | Once for that new filing | The policy's billing account, as a filing fee tied to the assessment |

## Hypothetical illustration

A driver's certificate lapsed after its SR-26 took effect. The certificate requires a new filing after a lapse, so a new filing is requested and its filing fee is assessed once and billed to the policy's billing account as a filing fee. The figures for any certificate are those in its fee schedule.
